summary: Frontend-only regression of the CSS display:none overlay-hiding micro-fix in TopNav.jsx (portal no longer unmounted while mobile drawer is open). Mobile 390x844: demo login OK, family SOS banner visible on /dashboard (1 card + global-sos-more pill), hidden on drawer open (wrapper computed display=none) and re-shown on close across 3 open/close cycles with zero console/page errors; drawer link m-safety navigated to /safety with a normal (non-forced) click. /safety: banners suppressed (count 0), sos-trigger-btn hit-testable (elementFromPoint returns sos-trigger-btn), single press produced exactly 1 POST /api/me/sos after the 3s arm countdown and rendered 'SOS sent to 1 contact'. Desktop 1920: banner renders on /dashboard (up to 3 cards + pill, wrapper display=contents), suppressed on /safety, single-fire panic = 1 POST, nav-assets-btn and nav-more-btn dropdowns open, admin login shows nav-admin. No demo SOS events were acknowledged (only the newly created test SOS remained un-acked; escalation cancel button was NOT clicked). Backend skipped per request.
critical_code_review_comments: Note for future tests/assertions: global-family-alarm's parentElement is now the wrapper <div style=display:contents> inside BODY, not BODY itself. Any assertion of parentElement.tagName === 'BODY' will fail even though rendering/stacking is unchanged (display:contents keeps layout identical).

TopNav.jsx is 274 lines and fine, but the overlay wrapper relies on mobileOpen state only; if another full-screen modal is added it will need the same treatment - consider a shared UI context flag instead of duplicating this pattern.
seed_data_creation: 2 real SOS events created for demo@neksathi.app while verifying single-fire panic button (1 mobile, 1 desktop). Not acknowledged.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_10 confirms the display:none overlay hiding has no regression vs iteration_9's unmount approach: drawer hides banners, links clickable with normal clicks, banners reappear on close, no remount/alarm retrigger errors, /safety panic single-fire OK on mobile+desktop. Panic button needs ~13-16s wait after click (3s arm countdown + geolocation 6s timeout + selfie capture) before the POST /api/me/sos fires - shorter waits give a false 0-request result. App ready for mobile build; no open frontend issues.
